mission_03: Differential Privacy (DP) provides mathematically rigorous privacy guarantees by ensuring that the output of an algorithm is nearly indistinguishable whether any individual's data is included or not. In federated learning, DP-FedAvg adds two key mechanisms: gradient clipping bounds the influence of any single client (sensitivity), and calibrated Gaussian noise obscures individual contributions. The clipping norm C limits how much any client's update can differ from the global model, while the noise multiplier sigma controls the noise scale. The privacy budget epsilon quantifies the total privacy loss across all training rounds, tracked using the moments accountant technique. This provides provable guarantees that an adversary cannot determine whether a specific client participated in training.
